newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE July canola ends limit up, feed grains lower.
newsitem.headline: WCE July canola ends limit up, feed grains lower.

text.p: WCE July canola futures closed up the $10.00 per tonne daily limit on light buying against strong seller resistance, traders said.
"There was just no July for sale," one canola trader said.
Much of the demand for canola was prompted by the gains in CBOT soybeans and soybean oil futures, traders said.
On Monday, July canola's daily limit will expand to $15.00 for three business days, while the $10.00 limit will remain for the other canola contracts, the Exchange said.
Some traders said that Canada's canola crop was developing well which may discourage additional gains.
Canola closed up $10.00 to down $1.70 with July at $373.00 and August up $4.30 at $353.90.
Flaxseed was lightly traded and closed narrowly mixed with July down $0.60 at $329.90 and September up $0.50 at $280.00.

Feed grains were pressured by forecasts for bountiful Canadian wheat and barley crops. Wheat closed down $0.70 to $1.40 with October off the most at $147.40. Barley was off $0.10 to $1.00 with October off $0.50 at $122.10.
Oats and feed peas did not trade.
(All values in Canadian dollars per tonne except oats and feed peas in U.S. dollars)
